html:
The Merina Kingdom was a state of the central highlands of Madagascar that, by the 1800s, ruled most of the island from Antananarivo. The map shows the highlands under this name from 1000 to 1815, long before the kingdom itself, which tradition says King Andriamanelo founded around 1540.

The Merina are highland rice farmers who built terraced paddies and walled hilltop villages. For two centuries their land was split among rival princes.

The rise to power:

  • Andrianampoinimerina, who ruled from about 1787 to 1810, reunited Imerina and made Antananarivo his capital. He is remembered for saying the sea would be the boundary of his rice field.
  • His son Radama I allied with Britain from 1817, gave up the slave trade in return for arms and training, and conquered much of the island. British missionaries wrote down Malagasy in the Latin alphabet and opened schools.
  • Ranavalona I, queen from 1828 to 1861, expelled the missionaries and persecuted Christians.
  • In 1869 Queen Ranavalona II and her prime minister were baptised, the conversion of the Merina court.

The kingdom built the wooden and stone palaces of the Rova. France attacked in 1883 and again in 1895, took Antananarivo, and in 1897 abolished the monarchy and exiled Queen Ranavalona III.
